83.t: Not capitalizing on his position; enjoying the music
83.s: He admits he did not take a piece of the action or exploit his publishing company, and took satisfaction from the music over money.
83.q: Oh, I'm sure I didn't. I'm sure I didn't. For instance, you know, if I'd have been like somebody who's going to do it, I'd have been getting a piece of the action all kinds of ways. You know, hey, I can get you on record. You've got to give me... Yeah. You know, which I didn't do. The only thing…

200.t: Family and making music for the right reasons
200.s: Allen says his grandchildren now like his work and that music is not about money but a product made from the heart.
200.q: When I was doing it I wasn’t making much money and stuff so everybody was — oh why don’t you do this to make some money. It wasn’t about money, it was about preparing the goods and then you sell it. Then you will spend your time making a product of work, then it will sell itself. You see what I…

407.t: Artistic vision, regrets, weddings and suffering
407.s: Carn would not do it all the same again, defends playing weddings, and rejects the idea that musicians must suffer.
407.q: Yeah. I hate to see those interviews, they say well look, just tell me if you had to do it all over again would you do the same thing? They said well yeah, really you know, I’d do the same thing. But I wouldn’t. You know? If I know what I know now, I wouldn’t do the same thing you know. But they…

803.t: Whether music must be a compulsion, and its rewards
803.s: He weighs the financial hardship against what music has given him: travel, people and joy.
803.q: I think as you get older as a musician and you realize that it is not an easy path. And I certainly look at my friends in Australia that I grew up with that didn’t end up being musicians but doing other things, and they’ve all got really nice houses and they’ve all got cars and they’ve all got…

322.t: Making it as a working musician and music as a calling
322.s: His goal was always to be a working musician; recalls Billy Mitchell's idea that music is a calling.
322.q: Good, good, good, good, good idea. My thing, my idea of making it, and to this day, from the time I was — I had specific numbers and everything in my head from the time I understood what was going on. But then and now is to be a working musician. And I know that sounds like an oxymoron but no,…

563.s: He hopes for more albums as leader, playing with heroes, finding his own voice, and a little more money.
563.q: Well I’m pretty happy with the way things are going. I’ve already gotten to do two albums of my own and I’ve played with some of my heroes. It’s not that I’ve done it all yet, I don’t mean that, but I’d like to continue to do more work as a leader perhaps and do more albums as a leader as well as…

748.t: Never seeking work, and Gil Evans and Mulligan as pure artists
748.s: Levin says work comes by word of mouth, admits doing jobs for money, and admires pure artists like Gil Evans.
748.q: Which is okay, it always has, there were very few periods that I can remember where I was really hurting for work. And in honesty I think I’m very fortunate but for the most part I’ve never gone looking for work, it’s been word of mouth and the phone usually rings. It’s good. I am very fortunate.…

721.t: Turning down work: ask for more money
721.s: He turns down jobs only for money and advises asking for more if you do not want a job.
721.q: I never turned down any for the last reason. I never turned down anything for that reason. If somebody wanted me to go out of town and didn’t offer me enough money I would turn it down.

104.s: She wants more money and dislikes motels with no room service.
104.q: Oh, well I’d like more money. I don’t know. I can’t think of one offhand. I mean it’s terrible I know I have some, but I can’t think of anything really serious except being put in a motel with no room service. That’s probably one of my most serious gripes.

656.t: Jazz is not about the money
656.s: Money should not be the criterion; some of his best playing was free gigs with Bill Holman.
656.q: It’s not about the bread. Everything can’t be about the money, it just can’t, especially not this, not the craft, not what you do, you can’t be about the bread. Yes you want to make it. Yes you want to be successful. But I’ll be damned if your criteria is how much money you make, you will not play…

216.t: Goals: what it means to make it
216.s: Discussing the opening of his book, Ricker says goals shift over a career; he once hoped to teach high school band in Denver.
216.q: Sure. What is the big deal for you. Well in my own case I’ll just say that when I started off in college, I wanted to be a, I thought if I could teach a high school band in Denver that’d be the greatest thing in the world. And that’s what I thought of doing. But it’s along the way I met people and,…

852.s: Making it means doing what you want and getting paid, accepting compromises.
852.q: Well you know for me making it is doing what you want and getting paid. Not just doing what you want and not getting paid. So — because we could do that. I could do that until the end of time in my living room, but yeah, being able to do things that you enjoy and making a living from it. And you…

165.t: Work as ministry, not chasing money
165.s: He sees his work as a ministry, says rewards are vanity, and chooses doing the work over chasing money.
165.q: Yes. It’s my ministry. It’s my ministry. I think to look for rewards for your work is vanity. I think that Salomon was correct when he said, “Vanity, vanity. All is vanity.” I think that those kind of things are vain. It’s better to do your work and pray that it helps someone else, than to look for…

372.t: Warne Marsh, the Tristano circle and making a living
372.s: Talk of Warne Marsh recordings and a book, the 'cult' view of Konitz, and his desire to work in the world rather than just practice.
372.ch: The Tristano group and leaving for Kenton
372.q: No, the man in Australia wrote a book called “Out of Nowhere” and assumed the voice of Warne Marsh, scarily so. He obviously knew Warne. He would have to [in order] to say the things he said . . . so close to home. But somehow or other, he had summed up that I had reached, as Warne Marsh, what I…

492.t: King Janaka parable and the artist's struggle
492.s: Lloyd tells of a man who leaves King Janaka rather than beg from a beggar and reflects that creative lives are hard.
492.ch: Higgins, Hendrix and the spiritual path
492.q: But if I was trying to go after gold mines, then I would miss the sound of what’s calling me, you understand? It’s like King Janaka - I’ll be quiet after this, I was trying to tell you - this guy knew King Janaka and he went to him and he wanted to borrow some bread. So he told the guy, “I need to…

381.t: Plans for the future and jazz as dance music
381.s: He will work as leader or sideman wherever the money is, and insists jazz should be danceable.
381.q: Well, I tell you -- I consider myself, I usually look upon myself as a prostitute -- wherever the money is, that's where I'm going. If I can make money as a leader, I mean if someone wants me to -- I'm not going to put myself in the position where I would be asking someone, but if someone thought…

452.t: Not materialistic: why he doesn't hoard money
452.s: Cobb says he wants only enough to live on, noting that Howard Hughes could not take his money with him.
452.q: I'm glad that I'm not materialistic, that material things don't destroy my life. I only need so much to live off of, don't need no more. And you think I (inaudible). You think I'd let it worry me. Just another (inaudible) break down try to get another one, same difference

120.t: Hating territory-band mute effects and not caring about money
120.s: He could not stand jerky wah-wah arrangements, tolerated theater bands because he was featured, and says happiness mattered more than pay.
120.ch: Looking back and the lean years
120.q: Oh, I couldn't take it - I just couldn't take it. Of course, I could stand the big theater orchestra because I got featured occasionally- blow and play ---
